headline: The Indonesia long-form's first subscribers are in: 3.2 per 1,000 views against 2 for the Asia long-form, on 60,467 views in 69 hours, so the Bali follow-up stays. The Tipu Short is due today with no script on disk; it lapses on 23 November.

top3.topic: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: due today, no script
top3.signal: The calendar's date for him is today, and a Tipu Jayanti row is in News18 Marathi on 19 November. The radar's step is to publish on the date, titled with the searched name “tipu sultan history”.
top3.recommendation: Decision 1: script and record today, publish by 22 November, judge on day three. If only one Short can be made before 24 November, make Tegh Bahadur and drop this one on the Today tab.

top3.signal: The top-ranked dated moment, four days out. The radar's step this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”. The calendar flags the martyrdom framing as one to avoid.
top3.recommendation: Decision 2: script by 21 November, record on 22, publish the evening of 23 November, judge on 26 November.

top3.topic: The Malay Ramayana Short, written 19 November
top3.signal: The Indonesia long-form runs at 875.5 views an hour. The Short on disk retells its strangest scene, Ravana's power granted by Allah, and hands off to it in the last line.
top3.recommendation: Record it this week and publish it between the two dated Shorts, with the long-form as its related video. That it sends viewers to the long-form is a guess.

more.topic: 4 December 1829, the sati ban: a script is already on disk
more.signal: The radar has Bentinck's regulation in 14 days. The wife-selling Short, written 17 September and never recorded, is built on that date: the year Britain banned sati, Englishmen were selling their wives at market.
more.recommendation: Clear its three VERIFY flags, record by 3 December and publish on 4 December. It rests on the date: the one sati Short so far, “How Missionaries Turned Sati Into a Fundraiser”, has 1,768 views.

skipped.signal: Hindi readership at 8x its 30-day median and English at 5.32x, five days after his birth anniversary, with a new song and a Parliament tribute in the news.
skipped.recommendation: Skip this week: two dated Shorts are already due, and freedom-fighter biographies have done below the usual here. If it is made later, the angle is the mission school he walked out of before he rose against the British, not his death.

skipped.topic: Two films on 4 December: Eetha and Maatrubhumi
skipped.signal: Eetha is a biopic with Shraddha Kapoor and Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace a war film with Salman Khan, both released 4 December. The data does not say who or what either film is about.
skipped.recommendation: Nothing until it is known who each film is about. Check by 27 November, when the radar's next step is due; if either is about a figure in the channel's lane, the plan is a Short between release day +1 and +9, judged on day three.

whats_working: “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana” runs at 875.5 views an hour; the Asia long-form has averaged 310.5 over its life. Its like rate is 1.8% against 0.9%, and on launch day it converted better too. Today is its day three.
Long-form still brings most of what uploads bring: 74.9% of upload-attributed net subscribers over 28 days, on 40.7% of upload views.

The best converter in the 90-day window is “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 13.1 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the Tipu Short's shape: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”
whats_wrong: Neither dated Short has a script on disk, and Tipu is due today. Probable cause: the owner's own picks take the week (Sonia Gandhi today; the Malay Ramayana, Thailand and Param Vir Chakra Shorts written since 19 November). Test: none. If only one dated Short can be made before 24 November, make Tegh Bahadur and drop Tipu on the Today tab so the list stays honest.

Film reach is not turning into subscribers: the Indonesia long-form 3.2 per 1,000 views, the Asia long-form 2, “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” 0.2. Long-form over the 365-day window has fallen out of its usual range to 8, and only 41.6% of November's long-form views were engaged views. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing, and videos that tour a story without convicting anyone. Test: the Indonesia video names who rewrote the story; compare its rate with the Asia one's on 22 November.

Long-form views fell 33.7% and watch time 38.3% week over week to 2026-11-17. Probable cause: the Asia long-form's Home-feed run ended, and the Indonesia launch has one day in the window (22,710 long-form views that day). Test: the week to 24 November.

The Ramayana film has stopped paying on Shorts: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule” has 1,669 views and “Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?” 1,385, both below the usual, while the film is still all over the news on its box office. Probable cause: two weeks after release the scene questions are answered. Test: none; no more film-answer Shorts.

actions.action: If not done yet, answer the Indonesian comments under “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana” in one pinned reply: where the Adam-and-Allah version comes from, and what Majapahit worshipped. /replies drafts it.
actions.rationale: The video is still climbing, so every new viewer reads its top comments, and two of the most-liked are from Java and Indonesia. That a reply helps is a guess.

actions.action: If not done yet, put the Indonesia long-form on the end screen and pinned comment of “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”, and make it the channel page's video for visitors who have not subscribed.
actions.rationale: The Asia long-form has 158,693 views on the same subject, and 915 subscribers over 28 days came from the channel page rather than any video. That either move helps is a guess.

actions.action: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” still has 0 views since 3 November, and the two Shorts published with it, “Itihasa vs Myth” (82) and “Is Caste Unique to India?” (255).
actions.rationale: A public Short gets at least a handful of views, so none at all points to its visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.

actions.action: Add the Google Analytics property number to the settings file.
actions.rationale: Without it the brief cannot say how itiha.info is doing. Search Console shows the site found on Google almost only for its own name.

growth.verdict: Needs 225 net subscribers a day. The channel does 47.54/day, so the target is a **4.7x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "1. scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1277 of the 2,902 subscribers that 22 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 25.1/day (704 of 1,236 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 22 long-form and 104 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.3 more long-form videos a year — 39.3 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 33 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 132, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 456 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 25.1/day (704 of 1,236 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 9 revision long-form videos, median 66 subscribers, against 33 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 25.1/day (704 of 1,236 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,277 subscribers on 72,973 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
